content: Before you start some work, always ask yourself three questions: Why am I doing it, What the results might be, and Will I be successful? Only when you think deeply and find satisfactory answers to these questions, go ahead.
author: Chanakya
explanation:
Impulsive action is the mother of regret. Chanakya, the supreme ancient master of statecraft, insisted on rigorous strategic foresight before committing resources, reputation, or time to any enterprise. Examining your underlying motive (Why), realistic consequences (What), and probability of execution (Will I succeed) filters out vanity projects and emotional miscalculations.

Clarity in the quiet room of planning guarantees strength on the field of execution.
practicalInsight: Before initiating a new project, investment, or difficult conversation today, write down candid answers to Chanakya's three questions.
reflectionPrompt: What current endeavor in your life are you pursuing without clear answers to why you are doing it and what the true outcome will be?
